title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review onboarding progress, confirm access and infra readiness, review early latency/cost metrics from pilot runs, and agree next steps for security checklist and benchmark run. AE recapped contract/pricing ask; SE walked through env issues (VPC peering, KMS key access) and tuning suggestions (batching, quantize config). Action items assigned for infra access and security docs.
topics: KMS / key management and audit logs
action_items: Michael Gomez: Provide VPC peering CIDR and open firewall rules to Redwood (due: 2026-06-07)
Priya Shah: Share sample prompt set and expected SLA targets (due: 2026-06-05)
Daniel Park (Redwood SE): Run second-run benchmark with adjusted batch size and send CSV (due: 2026-06-09)
Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE): Share pricing summary + Dedicated sizing proposal (due: 2026-06-06)
Sara Lewis: Coordinate legal for addendum with security controls and confirm timeline (due: 2026-06-10)
next_steps: Redwood to run tuned benchmark with quantized model variant and share results (Daniel)
Customer to provide VPC peering details and KMS ARN for access (Michael)
Redwood to send security docs (SOC2, ISO) and engineering runbook link
Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive next week focused on throughput tuning and rollout plan
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-03T15:00Z
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Head of ML, AstraWell), Michael Gomez (Infra Lead), Sara Lewis (Product)
Links shared: POC runbook (link: https://redwood.example/poc-runbook), benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/ASTRA-1)

Summary: quick check-in on onboarding progress; confirm infra access and run follow-up benchmark with tuning suggestions.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Lena Ortiz here, AE on the account. Daniel Park from SE is with me.
[00:00:12] Priya (AstraWell): Hi, Priya here. Michael and Sara on my side too. Sorry, running a bit late.
[00:00:20] Daniel (Redwood): No worries. We'll dive in — want to keep it to 40 minutes. Agenda is access status, early metrics, tuning recs, security items, and next steps.
[00:00:45] Michael (AstraWell): On access — we tried the VPC peering last night, looks like the traffic is getting dropped. We opened the firewall but maybe the route tables aren't right.
[00:01:10] Daniel (Redwood): Okay, timing out. Two quick checks — did you add the Redwood egress CIDRs we shared in the runbook, and did you accept the peering on your side? Sometimes peering acceptance step is missed.
[00:01:36] Michael (AstraWell): I thought we accepted, but let me double-check. We did add the CIDR, though I remember an error about overlapping ranges.
[00:01:55] Lena (Redwood): Overlap will drop routes. If you can share the CIDR ranges we can confirm; we can also propose a different subnet.
[00:02:15] Priya (AstraWell): Also on keys — we tried to give the KMS ARN for model encryption but IAM kept denying the PutKeyPolicy call.
[00:02:35] Daniel (Redwood): Yeah, typical IAM friction. We need the KMS key policy to allow Redwood service principal (we documented the role in the runbook). If you can add that policy or add us as a key user, that should unblock the tests.
[00:03:00] Michael (AstraWell): Got it. I'll escalate with infra and send the ARN and the policy snippet.
[00:03:18] Sara (AstraWell): Quick question on data retention — do we have audit logs for deduped requests? Our compliance team asked about log retention for forty five days.
[00:03:35] Lena (Redwood): Yes — by default logs are retained for 30 days on the hosted plan, but for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and push to your SIEM. We'll include the retention options in the security pack.
[00:03:55] Priya (AstraWell): Great. In the pilot metrics we saw token latency around 210ms average for small prompts, but tail latency spikes to 1200ms. Any thoughts?
[00:04:15] Daniel (Redwood): Do you have the run for exact model/version? Was that the quantized variant or FP16?
[00:04:30] Priya (AstraWell): That was the default we spun up via the GUI — I think the model was redwood-v1-large-quant? The name in the UI was a bit odd — "redcup v1 large" — might be transcription in the console.
[00:04:50] Daniel (Redwood): (laugh) yeah sometimes model aliasing in the UI is funky. The tail spikes often come from cold KV cache or from batches hitting a smaller GPU pool. Two quick levers: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts and increase batch timeout slightly to let the runtime combine requests.
[00:05:15] Lena (Redwood): Also, there's a Dedicated sizing option that gives steady throughput; we can propose a small reserved pool for the pilot to reduce spikes.
[00:05:35] Michael (AstraWell): For cost — our finance team flagged the per-token cost. How much savings with batching/quantization?
[00:05:50] Daniel (Redwood): You typically see 25-40% token-cost reduction with aggressive batching plus an INT8/quant variant depending on accuracy acceptance. We'll run a controlled benchmark to show tradeoffs.
[00:06:12] Priya (AstraWell): Accuracy matters — we can't drop beyond 2% for our intent extraction.
[00:06:25] Daniel (Redwood): Understood — we'll include accuracy metrics in the benchmark CSV; we'll run both FP16 and quant and compare.
[00:06:40] Sara (AstraWell): On security docs, can you re-share SOC2 and any third-party pen test summaries? Procurement asked for them yesterday.
[00:06:55] Lena (Redwood): Absolutely. I'll send the SOC2 pack and our SOC2 letter, plus the security runbook link. Also have the ISO outline.
[00:07:10] Michael (AstraWell): Back to VPC — do you support cross-account peering? Our infra is on a different account than the app.
[00:07:25] Daniel (Redwood): Yes, cross-account peering is supported; we just need the peering accept on the correct account and the route table entries. We'll include a step-by-step in the runbook.
[00:07:40] Priya (AstraWell): Regarding model variants, can Redwood fallback automatically if the Dedicated pool is saturated? We had a spike and a couple requests failed last night.
[00:07:55] Lena (Redwood): We have smart routing — you can set a fallback policy to a hosted variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost; that avoids errors. We'll propose a canary/fallback strategy.
[00:08:12] Daniel (Redwood): For the benchmark run, I suggest we run three passes: 1) current config, 2) with prefix caching enabled, 3) with quantized model and adjusted batch size. We'll capture P99 latency and token cost per 1k tokens.
[00:08:35] Michael (AstraWell): Sounds good. Do you need any traffic scripts from us? We have a synthetic traffic generator but it's behind the corp VPC.
[00:08:50] Daniel (Redwood): If you can provide a sample traffic script or we can drive traffic from Redwood to the endpoint. Either works but if it's internal-only we can accept a sanitized replay.
[00:09:10] Priya (AstraWell): We'll share a replay file and the prompt set.
[00:09:20] Sara (AstraWell): Any updates on rate limits? We had a 429 last week during a batch test.
[00:09:35] Lena (Redwood): That was likely due to the default quota on the hosted endpoint. If you anticipate sustained throughput, Dedicated or raising the quota is an option. We'll include quota guidance and cost implications in the sizing doc.
[00:09:55] Daniel (Redwood): Also check if the client retries were aggressive — exponential backoff helps with a 429 flood.
[00:10:10] Priya (AstraWell): For the IAM/KMS policy snippet, do you have an example in the runbook?
[00:10:25] Daniel (Redwood): Yes, runbook has a policy snippet; I'll paste it into the channel after the call. Note there were a couple typos in the doc earlier (we had "key: redwood-service" which should be the full ARN).
[00:10:40] Michael (AstraWell): Great. On metrics we noticed a higher cost per 1k tokens when requests included longer context, is that expected?
[00:10:55] Daniel (Redwood): Yes, cost scales with context size and KV cache effectiveness. If you can trim context or use cached embeddings for longer histories, that will help.
[00:11:20] Priya (AstraWell): Can Redwood integrate with our embeddings store? We're using Pinecone for retrieval.
[00:11:35] Lena (Redwood): We can. Many customers use Pinecone — we have examples in the repo. Note that using an external store adds network latency; we can run end-to-end tests.
[00:11:55] Priya (AstraWell): Good to know.
[00:12:10] Daniel (Redwood): Quick note on quantization — INT8 variants sometimes change tokenization side-effects slightly. We'll include per-class accuracy checks.
[00:12:25] Michael (AstraWell): For the Dedicated sizing you mentioned, any ballpark monthly price for a pilot? Finance needs an estimate.
[00:12:40] Lena (Redwood): Ballpark — small reserved pool for pilot might be $8-12k/month depending on GPU type and commit. I'll send a more precise number after we know target QPS and average token length.
[00:12:58] Sara (AstraWell): Ok, for timelines we want pilot to be production-ready by end of month. Is that realistic?
[00:13:12] Daniel (Redwood): Depending on infra readiness — if VPC and KMS are done this week we can run the final benchmark next week and start a canary rollout. I'd say it's realistic if access is fully provisioned.
[00:13:30] Priya (AstraWell): We'll prioritize KMS and peering this week.
[00:13:40] Michael (AstraWell): I'll open a ticket and share the peering CIDR and firewall rule screenshot by tomorrow EOD.
[00:13:52] Lena (Redwood): Thanks. Daniel, do you want to walk through the benchmark plan now?
[00:14:05] Daniel (Redwood): Sure — we'll run the three passes I mentioned. For each pass we collect: median latency, P95, P99, tokens processed, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy on the prompt set. We'll attach the CSV to the sheet and annotate rows where we changed batch size or cache settings.
[00:14:28] Priya (AstraWell): For batch sizes — what's the recommended starting point? We're seeing timeouts when we set batch to 64.
[00:14:42] Daniel (Redwood): Start at batch 8-16 and increment; large batches can increase latency for single-request patterns. Also increase the batching window slightly (e.g., 20-50ms) to let the system coalesce requests.
[00:15:00] Priya (AstraWell): Noted. Can you show the config flag names?
[00:15:10] Daniel (Redwood): The flags are in the runbook — "batch_size_limit", "batch_window_ms", and "prefix_cache_enabled: true/false". In our console the UI labels them as "batching.max_batch" and "batching.window_ms" occasionally, the naming's been inconsistent.
[00:15:35] Michael (AstraWell): On network egress — do you provide egress IPs for whitelisting or is it dynamic?
[00:15:48] Lena (Redwood): We provide a set of egress CIDRs for hosted and can provide a more static range for Dedicated/private deployments. We'll double-check the exact list and send it.
[00:16:05] Sara (AstraWell): Any compliance red flags we should be aware of? Our security team does data residency checks.
[00:16:20] Lena (Redwood): We can localize in specific regions for data residency or offer private deployment. We'll include region options and the private deployment checklist in the security pack.
[00:16:36] Priya (AstraWell): Great. For the benchmark cadence — when will you run it?
[00:16:45] Daniel (Redwood): If we have VPC and KMS access by Friday, I can run the first two passes Friday night and the quantized run early next week. Results by Monday morning.
[00:16:55] Michael (AstraWell): I'll try to get the access by EOD Thursday.
[00:17:05] Lena (Redwood): Perfect. Quick note on billing — if you do Dedicated pilot for 30 days we can do a short-term commit to limit costs. I'll include that option in the pricing doc.
[00:17:20] Priya (AstraWell): One more question — do you have alerting for drift in accuracy? Our product team needs regression alerts.
[00:17:35] Daniel (Redwood): Yes, we have quality monitoring and can tie alerts to eval prompt sets; we can set threshold-based alerts and attach to Slack or pager. We'll demo that in the deep dive.
[00:17:55] Sara (AstraWell): Ok, anything else from the customer side?
[00:18:05] Priya (AstraWell): No, that's it for now.
[00:18:10] Michael (AstraWell): I'll add the infra ticket and send screenshots.
[00:18:18] Lena (Redwood): Great. Recap of action items: Michael sends VPC CIDR and firewall screenshots; Priya sends prompt set and accuracy targets; Daniel runs benchmarks and shares CSV; Lena sends pricing and security docs; Sara coordinates legal.
[00:18:45] Daniel (Redwood): I'll also paste the exact KMS policy snippet in the Slack channel after this call — there was a small typo in the runbook we corrected.
[00:19:00] Priya (AstraWell): Appreciate it.
[00:19:05] Lena (Redwood): We'll schedule the technical deep-dive for next week — propose Tue 10am PT?
[00:19:15] Michael (AstraWell): Tue 10am PT works.
[00:19:20] Sara (AstraWell): Works for me.
[00:19:25] Priya (AstraWell): Works.
[00:19:30] Lena (Redwood): Okay we'll send calendar invite and include the runbook and benchmark sheet. Thanks everyone.
[00:19:40] Michael (AstraWell): Thanks. Bye.
[00:19:45] Priya (AstraWell): Bye.

Notes: Some transcription artifacts (model name aliasing, runbook typos) — corrected by SE in chat. References: POC runbook link, benchmark sheet link.
